## S14. Differential expression, pathways and normal tissue: details

**camera check of the Hallmark results** **(Table S26)**.

```{r camcount, include = FALSE}
camn <- gs5 |> filter(collection == "Hallmark") |> select(comparator, adjustment, pathway, padj) |>
  left_join(cam5 |> pivot_wider(id_cols = c(comparator, adjustment, pathway), names_from = correlation, values_from = FDR),
            by = c("comparator", "adjustment", "pathway")) |>
  group_by(comparator, adjustment) |> summarise(f = sum(padj < 0.05), d = sum(Default < 0.05), e = sum(Estimated < 0.05), .groups = "drop")
cn <- \(c, a, k) camn[[k]][camn$comparator == c & camn$adjustment == a]
```

Of the 50 Hallmark sets, fgsea calls `r cn("C1-C3", "Unadjusted", "f")` (unadjusted) and `r cn("C1-C3", "Purity-adjusted", "f")` (purity-adjusted) significant vs. C1–C3, and `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Unadjusted", "f")` and `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Purity-adjusted", "f")` vs. C5 ERBB2-high. camera with the default correlation keeps `r cn("C1-C3", "Unadjusted", "d")`, `r cn("C1-C3", "Purity-adjusted", "d")`, `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Unadjusted", "d")` and `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Purity-adjusted", "d")`; with the estimated correlation, `r cn("C1-C3", "Unadjusted", "e")`, `r cn("C1-C3", "Purity-adjusted", "e")`, `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Unadjusted", "e")` and `r cn("C5 ERBB2-high", "Purity-adjusted", "e")`. Estimated correlations are high for strongly co-expressed programs (vs. C1–C3, unadjusted: E2F targets `r f2(cam5$Correlation[cam5$correlation == "Estimated" & cam5$comparator == "C1-C3" & cam5$adjustment == "Unadjusted" & cam5$pathway == "E2F_TARGETS"])`, allograft rejection `r f2(cam5$Correlation[cam5$correlation == "Estimated" & cam5$comparator == "C1-C3" & cam5$adjustment == "Unadjusted" & cam5$pathway == "ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION"])`, vs. `r f2(cam5$Correlation[cam5$correlation == "Estimated" & cam5$comparator == "C1-C3" & cam5$adjustment == "Unadjusted" & cam5$pathway == "ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY"])` for early estrogen response), which shrinks their effective number of genes. With the strict setting, only early estrogen response (both models), glycolysis and mTORC1 signalling (purity-adjusted) remain significant vs. C1–C3, and nothing vs. C5 ERBB2-high. The default setting keeps most fgsea results.

**Step 4 genes in pathway leading edges.** For each significant Hallmark set (unadjusted model), the leading edge is the subset of its genes that drives the enrichment. Stable Step 4 genes (selected in ≥70% of training sets) fall in the leading edges of `r sum(le5$comparator == "C1-C3")` sets vs. C1–C3, and only PSMD3 (an amplicon gene, in MYC targets) vs. C5 ERBB2-high **(Table S27)**. Strongly differential genes almost always sit in leading edges, so this annotates the genes rather than adding evidence.

**The 8 key genes across comparisons** **(Table S28)**. The 7 compact-model genes differ from luminal tumors but barely from C5 ERBB2-high; ERBB2 and STARD3 do the reverse. Against matched normal tissue, all 7 move as they do against luminal tumors.

**Reactome** **(Table S30)**.

- **vs. C1–C3:** unadjusted, the top pathways are immune: neutrophil degranulation, lymphoid–non-lymphoid immunoregulatory interactions, interleukin signalling and antigen cross-presentation. After purity adjustment, they are translation, respiratory electron transport and DNA replication, the finer form of the Hallmark proliferation and metabolism sets. Estrogen-dependent gene expression is lower in both models.
- **vs. C5 ERBB2-high:** cell-cycle checkpoints, M phase and DNA replication are lower in both models; immune pathways (including IL-10 and IL-4/IL-13 signalling) are higher only without adjustment.

Reactome results use fgsea only and share its inflated p-values.

**Tumor vs. matched normal tissue.** `r sum(table(pairs51$patient_id, pairs51$plate) == 2)` of the `r n_distinct(pairs51$patient_id)` pairs were sequenced on the same plate. The tumors come from sites BH (6), E9 (4) and GI (1), and their PAM50 mix is similar to the rest of the group. Normal samples come almost entirely from the early processing era (Section 1.3), so plate and era effects are partly paired out but not removed. Pathways are in **(Figure S9)** and paired immune and stromal cell scores in **(Table S29)**.

knitr::include_graphics(file.path(r51, "hallmark_nes.png"))
```

```{=html}
<!-- Cross-references: in-text (Figure/Table X) citations link to the item; captions link back to each citation -->
<style>
  .xref-target:target, .xref-target.flash { outline: 3px solid #f0ad4e; outline-offset: 4px; }
  a.xref:target { background: #fff3cd; }
  .backrefs { font-size: 0.85em; margin-left: 0.4em; }
  .backrefs a { margin-left: 0.3em; text-decoration: none; }
  /* Contents panel toggle */
  #toc-toggle { position: fixed; top: 8px; left: 8px; z-index: 1000; padding: 3px 9px; font-size: 13px;
                border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px; background: #fff; cursor: pointer; }
  #toc-toggle:hover { background: #f3f3f3; }
  body.toc-hidden #TOC { display: none; }
  body.toc-hidden .toc-content { width: 100%; }
</style>
<button id="toc-toggle" type="button" title="Show or hide the contents panel">Hide contents</button>
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  // Contents panel toggle (choice remembered in this browser when storage is available)
  const btn = document.getElementById("toc-toggle");
  const tocCol = document.getElementById("TOC")?.parentElement;
  const setToc = hidden => { document.body.classList.toggle("toc-hidden", hidden); if (tocCol) tocCol.style.display = hidden ? "none" : ""; btn.textContent = hidden ? "Show contents" : "Hide contents"; };
  try { setToc(localStorage.getItem("tocHidden") === "1"); } catch (e) { setToc(false); }
  btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const hidden = !document.body.classList.contains("toc-hidden"); setToc(hidden);
    try { localStorage.setItem("tocHidden", hidden ? "1" : "0"); } catch (e) {}
  });
  const key = s => s.trim().replace(/\s+/g, "-").toLowerCase();   // "Figure S1" -> "figure-s1"
  const back = {};
  // Anchor each figure/table caption
  document.querySelectorAll("p.caption, caption").forEach(c => {
    const m = c.textContent.match(/^\s*(Figure|Table)\s+(S?\d+)\./);
    if (!m) return;
    const box = c.tagName === "CAPTION" ? c.closest("table") : (c.closest(".figure") || c.parentElement);
    box.id = key(m[1] + " " + m[2]); box.classList.add("xref-target");
    back[box.id] = document.createElement("span"); back[box.id].className = "backrefs";
    c.appendChild(back[box.id]);
  });
  // Section targets for "Supplement S4"
  const sec = {};
  document.querySelectorAll("h2, h3").forEach(h => {
    const m = h.textContent.match(/^\s*(S\d+)\./); const s = h.closest(".section");
    if (m && s) sec[m[1]] = s.id;
  });
  // Link bold citations in the text
  let k = 0;
  document.querySelectorAll("strong").forEach(s => {
    if (s.closest("caption, p.caption")) return;
    const t = s.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, " ");
    if (!/^\(.*\)$/.test(t)) return;
    s.innerHTML = t.replace(/(Figure|Table)\s+(S?\d+)|Supplement\s+(S\d+)/g, (all, kind, num, sup) => {
      const target = sup ? sec[sup] : key(kind + " " + num);
      if (!target || (!sup && !back[target])) return all;
      const ref = "ref-" + (++k);
      if (!sup) back[target].insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<a href="#${ref}" title="Back to text">↩${back[target].childElementCount + 1}</a>`);
      return `<a class="xref" id="${ref}" href="#${target}">${all}</a>`;
    });
  });
  // Literature citations: [n] / [n, m] in the text link to reference n; each reference links back
  const refSec = document.getElementById("references");
  if (!refSec) return;
  const bib = {};
  refSec.querySelectorAll("ol > li").forEach((li, i) => {
    li.id = "bib-" + (i + 1); li.classList.add("xref-target");
    bib[i + 1] = document.createElement("span"); bib[i + 1].className = "backrefs"; li.appendChild(bib[i + 1]);
  });
  const walker = document.createTreeWalker(document.querySelector(".main-container") || document.body, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT, {
    acceptNode: n => /\[\d+(\s*,\s*\d+)*\]/.test(n.nodeValue) && !n.parentElement.closest("#references, a, code, pre, script, style")
      ? NodeFilter.FILTER_ACCEPT : NodeFilter.FILTER_REJECT });
  const nodes = []; while (walker.nextNode()) nodes.push(walker.currentNode);
  let c = 0;
  nodes.forEach(n => {
    const span = document.createElement("span");
    span.innerHTML = n.nodeValue.replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;")
      .replace(/\[(\d+(?:\s*,\s*\d+)*)\]/g, (all, nums) => "[" + nums.split(/\s*,\s*/).map(num => {
        if (!bib[num]) return num;
        const id = "cite-" + (++c);
        bib[num].insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend", `<a href="#${id}" title="Back to text">↩${bib[num].childElementCount + 1}</a>`);
        return `<a class="xref" id="${id}" href="#bib-${num}">${num}</a>`;
      }).join(", ") + "]");
    n.replaceWith(...span.childNodes);
  });
});
</script>
```
